key_insight: Draw towers make km of structured multimaterial fiber with no litho; a 1D substrate is a genuinely different capital model for passive or coarse electronics.
killer_doubt: Woven crossings at >=10 um fiber pitch give ~1e6 bits/cm2 per layer versus DRAM ~1e10; amorphous chalcogenide mobility ~1e-3-1 cm2/Vs cannot drive ns access.
decisive_experiment: Draw one chalcogenide/polymer/metal FET fiber (university draw tower, ~$150k); measure Ion/Ioff, switching time and minimum continuous feature; kill if Ion <1 uA at 1 V or features break up below 100 nm.
prior_art: Fink lab (MIT) multimaterial fiber devices; Bayindir/Yaman iterative-draw chalcogenide nanowires; none found as DRAM-class memory.

key_insight: Coarse 193 nm guides plus BCP self-assembly can define 10-30 nm dot lattices with no EUV; defect remapping at test makes per-site defectivity tolerable.
killer_doubt: A single rectifying Schottky diode passes charge one way, so cannot write both 0 and 1; a 5 nm MIM dot holds ~0.05-0.1 fF (~400 e-) even at AR ~20.
decisive_experiment: SIS-convert a PS-b-PDMS dot array on TiN and measure single-dot I-V by conductive AFM (~$100k): need rectification >1e4 at 1 V and reverse leakage <1 fA; then prove a bidirectional write path.
prior_art: Our B2-11/N-30 DSA honeycomb and B2-20 SIS lamellae (ALIVE); imec 37 nm BCP contact multiplication; 1D1C crosspoint proposals.

key_insight: If data dies before the bit decays, refresh is never needed: retention can be a per-allocation contract rather than a 6-sigma cell spec.
killer_doubt: Refresh-free capacity is capped at bandwidth x lifetime: 3.35 TB/s x 2 ms ~7 GB/GPU; sub-ms temporaries already stay in SRAM; poly-Si tail ~0.2-5 pA misses ms.
decisive_experiment: Instrument the PyTorch/CUDA allocator on LLM training and serving (~$50k) and histogram HBM bytes by lifetime; go if >30% of capacity-time dies within the retention target. Then switch the cell to IGZO, tuned to 1-10 s.
prior_art: Flikker/RAIDR-style retention-aware refresh; Kioxia/IMECAS 3D IGZO gain cells; lifetime-typed ephemeral memory tier not found.

key_insight: A 1e4x thermal draw shrinks a cm preform of coaxial gate stacks to nm pitch in one step; slicing makes vertical GAA arrays with no patterning tool.
killer_doubt: Coaxial cylinders break up by Plateau-Rayleigh below ~100 nm (tau ~ eta*r/gamma ~0.1 s at r=10 nm); a 3 nm dielectric must hold ±0.3 nm over km.
decisive_experiment: Two-stage draw of a 7-element coaxial As2Se3/glass/Sn preform to <=50 nm cores (~$200k); microtome 100 nm slices and probe gated I-V. Kill if gate continuity <99% or Ion/Ioff <1e6.
prior_art: Fink lab in-fiber devices and capillary breakup; Yaman et al. iterative draw of ~15 nm chalcogenide nanowires; no sliced transistor arrays found.

key_insight: Folding a single membrane processed once in a planar flow gives single-crystal access FETs in every layer; fold-edge wiring replaces TSVs.
killer_doubt: Fold radius >=33 um gives >=67 um layer pitch: an HBM-style stack, not 3D tiers; 26 layers at 90% each yield 0.9^26 = 6.5% without known-good-die.
decisive_experiment: Fold a 5-layer 2 um SOI test membrane with neutral-plane Cu hinge lines (~$150k); measure wire yield and resistance through 1,000 -40/125 C cycles, plus continuity of a 1 um-pitch fold bus.
prior_art: Our own B3-15/N-54 origami stack (ALIVE, same mechanism); imec W2W hybrid bonding at ~300 nm pitch interconnects better.

key_insight: CMOS-under-array tile sense amps keep refresh traffic off global bitlines, so bandwidth survives even very short retention.
killer_doubt: 10 pA on ~1 fF gives ~20 us retention; ~5 fJ per local refresh is ~2 W/GB versus DDR5 ~12 mW/GB; oxide TFTs are equally cheap and leak <1 aA.
decisive_experiment: No hardware needed: SPICE a 4k-cell tile with 1 fF local bitlines and measured LTPS/IGZO Ioff tails; compute standby W/GB. Kill if >100 mW/GB, which first-order numbers predict.
prior_art: Gain-cell eDRAM with local refresh; CMOS-under-array (Micron CuA); IGZO 2T0C gives the same cheap stacked tiers without leakage.

key_insight: Self-limiting 1.5-3 nm oxide skins print at room temperature with no ALD or epitaxy tool; liquid-metal In2O3/ITO variants make working TFTs.
killer_doubt: Retention is already interface-limited: IGZO is <1 aA, 1e2-3e4 s. As-printed Ga2O3 skin is amorphous with poor mobility. Printing coats only planar tiers, and planar 2T0C never beats vertical density.
decisive_experiment: Print Ga2O3 and In2O3 skins on 100 mm wafers (~$80k); map thickness and Vt sigma; build 2T0C cells and compare retention at 85 C with ALD IGZO. Kill if not >10x better.
prior_art: Zavabeti/Kalantar-Zadeh (RMIT) liquid-metal printed 2D oxides, Science 2017; printed 2D In2O3/ITO transistors; ALD IGZO/IGO gain cells.

key_insight: Mirror-bit NROM shows that spatially separate trapped-charge pockets with reverse read can store several bits per gate crossing.
killer_doubt: Hot-carrier charge trapping endures ~1e5 cycles against a 3e8-7e13 need, and writes take us. N-type oxide channels have no holes, so NROM hot-hole erase is impossible.
decisive_experiment: Fabricate an IGZO/SiN-nanodot front/back-gated transistor (~$150k); cycle program/erase at <=50 ns to 1e9 at 85 C. Kill if the window collapses before 1e8 or no erase works without holes.
prior_art: Saifun/Spansion MirrorBit NROM (2-4 bits/cell), 3D charge-trap NAND; our N-10 direct-tunnel 3D AND is the better quasi-volatile version.

key_insight: Writes go through a transistor channel (endurance-safe) and reads are non-destructive; one series read channel replaces 8-16 read FETs and contacts, mapping onto NAND-style vertical holes.
killer_doubt: Pass-boost must lift unselected ~0.2 fF nodes >1.5 V (plate coupling >=0.6) without over-stressing 5-8 nm read oxide; ~30 nm-pitch neighbour coupling may eat a 200 mV window.
decisive_experiment: Planar 8-node IGZO string on a university line (~$300k): each floating gate gets its own IGZO write FET and plate line. Measure read margin versus pattern, boost disturb, read time on 50 fF, and retention at 85 C.
prior_art: Japanese oxide-semiconductor NAND gain-cell patents (US8421071, US8750023, US12082391: series cells, floating nodes, OS write FETs) (via search snippet); IMECAS vertical 2T0C.

key_insight: Retention-tail statistics are the hidden data moat; pooled ppm-scale tail maps across many fabs could rank tail mechanisms, especially for oxide channels.
killer_doubt: 1 um devices miss the nanoscale GIDL/trap-assisted tunnelling fields that set the Si tail, so transfer is doubtful. 1e8 cells/yr reaches only ~5.5 sigma against a 6-sigma at 1e10 need.
decisive_experiment: Pilot with 2-3 NNCI fabs (~$600k): the same IGZO 2T0C retention-tail macro at 1 um and 100 nm Lg, with 1e6 cells each. Test whether the tail shape scales; if it does not, 1 um shuttles are moot.
prior_art: NNCI university nanofab network, Natcast/NSTC prototyping, SkyWater SKY130 open PDK, DoD Microelectronics Commons; no open retention-tail database found.

key_insight: A node-gated top-up path refreshes all cells in parallel with zero row activations, which removes refresh bandwidth loss and refresh-induced hammer.
killer_doubt: Bulk photocarriers reach every junction: at 1 W/cm2 a 0-node collects ~0.1-1 pA versus a 13 fA budget; PD plus gating FET doubles the 6F2 cell.
decisive_experiment: Simulate first, then a 180 nm BSI test chip (~$250k): 1T1C plus PD plus gating-FET cells under pulsed LED, measuring 0-node upset rate and 1-node restore at 85 C. Benchmark it against an electrical refresh-rail pulse.
prior_art: Self-restoring 3T/4T dynamic cells with a global refresh rail do this electrically; BSI image-sensor pixels; no optical-refresh DRAM found.

key_insight: A 4F2 transistor-free crosspoint, with two KrF masks per deck and 64 decks, is the cheapest conceivable patterning if a two-terminal access device could hold charge.
killer_doubt: Half-select OTS leakage ~0.1-1 nA on 1 fF gives ~us retention: ~100 fJ x 1e5/s is ~80 W/GB; 10 years is ~3e13 firings versus ~1e8-1e11 reported.
decisive_experiment: 1S1C coupons (~$100k): measure node droop through an OTS at V/2 bias, the stored window loss to Vhold, and endurance to 1e11 firings. Kill if retention <1 ms or endurance <1e12.
prior_art: Intel/Micron 3D XPoint OTS selectors; academic 1S1C selector-capacitor crossbar concepts (not verified here).
